2013_057_120313mtg.paragraph: Board of Education regular-meeting packet for the Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, for the meeting held December 3, 2013 at 7:00 PM at Troy High School, 4777 Northfield Pkwy. It carries the agenda, the November 12 and November 19, 2013 minutes, the October 2013 Treasurer's Report and check register, an October year-to-date Fiscal Year 2014 budget report, a TEA negotiations update, and a state-accountability report. The central action is authorization of a first series of bonds, the 2014 School Building and Site Bonds, in an amount not to exceed $56,000,000 against the $125,000,000 proposal approved by voters November 5, 2013.

**Meeting and packet**

Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, December 3, 2013, 7:00 PM, Troy High School, 4777 Northfield Pkwy., Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools; public comment is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker. Agenda: recognitions (CAPE Steering Committee for Bond 2013; student representative from Niles Community High School), consent agenda, negotiations update, Top to Bottom rankings, the 2014 School Building and Site Bonds, cancellation of the December 17, 2013 workshop, a bond projects timeline, and a closed session on negotiations.

**Negotiations, accountability and bonds**

Jasen Witt reported that the District and the TEA had met 32 times as of November 25, 2013, that a fact-finder was mutually selected October 31, 2013, and that hearings were set for January 23 and 24, 2014 with February 26, 2014 in reserve. Anne Mull reviewed the Michigan School Accountability Scorecard and Top to Bottom rankings released in August 2013, including Troy High's move from Continuous Improvement to Focus. The Board considered a resolution issuing the 2014 School Building and Site Bonds in an amount not to exceed $56,000,000 by negotiated sale, with Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated as senior managing underwriter, Clark Hill PLC as bond counsel and Stauder, Barch & Associates, Inc. as financial advisor.

Many teachers, parents and residents spoke on the unsettled TEA contract, including Kerry Brennan (a banner with over 300 parent signatures), Cal Mott (Uniserv director from 1999 through 2013) and TEA president Tony Lucchi.

**Item 6.A, Negotiations Update.** Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources; no action required. Negotiations with the TEA began March 2013; a state mediator was engaged May 2013; agreements were reached with TESPA (Para-Educators/Skilled Trades) and TESA (Secretaries) in June 2013; the TEA filed its Petition for Fact-Finding June 28, 2013; the contract expired June 30, 2013; a fact-finder was mutually selected October 31, 2013; as of November 25, 2013 the teams had met 32 times, with 4 formal economic proposal options from the District and 3 from the TEA. Next mediation Wednesday, December 11, 2013; pre-hearing conference November 18, 2013; hearings January 23 and 24, 2014 and February 26, 2014 if needed; post-hearing briefs 30 days after close of hearing (late March 2014); non-binding recommendations 21 days later (mid/late April 2014); a 60-day minimum bargaining period follows (May/June 2014).

**Item 7.A, Accountability Update Fall 2013.** Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment. In August 2013 the Michigan Department of Education released the Michigan School Accountability Scorecards, the Top to Bottom ranking and the Reward, Focus and Priority lists under NCLB flexibility from the U.S. Department of Education; Adequate Yearly Progress will no longer be reported. Annual Measureable Objectives run from the 2011-2012 proficiency rate toward an end proficiency rate of 85% by 2021-2022 in a five color system. Statewide green districts include 38 single school entities, 23 new districts and 15 small districts with fewer than 30 students tested; green schools include 73 new schools and 22 small schools; county examples are Novi Adult Ed (approximately 6 students assessed), Oxford Virtual Academy and the Kennedy Center in Pontiac. Focus schools turn on the gap between average scale scores of the top 30% and bottom 30%; Reward schools sit in the top 5%. From 2012-2013 to 2013-2014 Troy High moved from Continuous Improvement to Focus and Costello from Reward to Continuous Improvement, while Barnard, Bemis, Boulan Park, Hamilton, Larson, Leonard and Wattles moved to Reward but remain Focus on the 4 year cohort; Baker, Morse, Smith and Troy Union remained Focus; Hill, Schroeder and Wass remained Reward; Martell and Niles remained Continuous Improvement. The bottom 30% subgroup shows 0% proficient until overall proficiency exceeds 70%, and an AMO of 33% translates into 80% overall; Michigan schools with 2013-14 AMOs below 70% are 58% reading, 89% writing, 95% math, 98% social studies, 99.8% science.

**Item 8.A, 2014 School Building and Site Bonds.** The $125,000,000 bond issue was passed by voters November 5, 2013; the first series is not to exceed $56,000,000, with Dr. Barbara Fowler and Mark S. Rajter authorized to accept a purchase offer. The resolution recites preliminary qualification of $125,000,000 from the Michigan Department of Treasury under Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005, enacted pursuant to Section 16, Article IX of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, with final qualification sought on Treasury Form 3451 (Rev. 03-13) through the Michigan School Bond Qualification and Loan Program. Purposes: remodeling and equipping buildings to enhance security, technology equipment and infrastructure, additions, site improvements and school buses. Bonds are dated as of delivery in denominations of $5,000 or multiples, maturing the first day of May, interest payable May 1 and November 1 with record dates April 15 and October 15, CUSIP 897404, registered to Cede & Co. as nominee of the Depository Trust Company. Taxes may be levied without limitation as to rate or amount under Article IX, Sections 6 and 16, into a 2014 School Building and Site Bonds Debt Retirement Fund. The negotiated sale names Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated as senior managing underwriter, Clark Hill PLC as bond counsel and Stauder, Barch & Associates, Inc. as financial advisor, with ratings possible from Moody's Investors Service, Fitch Ratings and/or Standard & Poor's. Exhibit A, the bond form under Act 451, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976 and Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, is signed by Nancy Philippart, President, and countersigned by Paula Fleming, Secretary. Exhibit C, the Continuing Disclosure Agreement under SEC Rule 15c2-12, requires the annual report by the 180th day after fiscal year end beginning with the year ending June 30, 2014, filed to EMMA, plus notice of any of 14 listed events within ten business days. Form 3451 commits the District to certify and levy its debt millage annually and file an Annual Loan Activity Statement.

**Items 10.A, 10.B and 11.A.** A resolution cancelling the December 17, 2013 Board of Education Workshop; Dr. Fowler's report on 2013 bond projects (high school auditorium design, secure entries at elementary and middle schools, instructional equipment, Athens classroom additions, Troy High classroom, band room and performing arts storage additions, and traffic site visits); and a resolution entering closed session on negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(c), roll call of Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt and Underwood.
